findings: run.batch_target.* (4 rows, section 9.6): Go now passes all four by refusing the launch. In each row and in each of the 5 fix-round and reviewer runs, all 16 arguments were refused (exit 127, child never ran, no file created): 16 of 16 per row, 64 of 64 across the four rows per run. Baseline of the frozen build (38b6b72), per row: path with a space {"INJECTED": 8, "argument_changed": 2, "other": 5, "received_exactly": 1}; path without a space {"INJECTED": 8, "argument_changed": 2, "received_exactly": 6}; every baseline case exited 1.

Mechanism (read from the committed diff of 84c7665 when this record was written): run.Run calls refuseTarget(path) on the path resolved by PATH lookup, before exec.Command. On Windows refuseTarget trims trailing dots and spaces from the last path component, lowercases the extension and refuses .bat and .cmd with exit 127, a stderr message and meta CHILD_LAUNCH_FAILED; on Unix it returns no refusal. Go therefore does not escape batch arguments at all: it cannot launch batch files (the section 9.6 text allows escaping or refusal).

Non-gating run.cmd_metachar_argument went fail -> pass (baseline: injected=true; now exit 127, cmd_script_ran=false, injected=false). run.cmd_metachar_argument_nospace_path stays pass but its observation changed from the batch file running (exit 1) to a refusal (exit 127). The info row resolution.pathext_cmd changed from cmd.exe running (exit 1) to a refusal (exit 127, cmd_ran=false): a bare name resolved through PATHEXT to a .cmd is refused as well.

Because cmd.exe is no longer started by heimdall-proto, the owner's cmd.exe AutoRun no longer runs in the batch rows. The harness control run.batch_control still records a plain cmd.exe /c (no /d, no heimdall-proto) exiting 1 with 94 stderr bytes on this host.

Every other row keeps its baseline verdict and gating flag (89 of 94 rows incl. the 5 host rows). Still not passing and non-gating: agent.client_identifiable_by_server (fixture agent gets error 1347, ERROR_CANT_OPEN_ANONYMOUS, i.e. the client connected at SecurityAnonymous) and tui.ctrl_c_event (exit 1 instead of 130; terminal restored, alternate screen not left active). Both are recorded, not gated, under section 9.6.

K14 on Windows (unchanged from the baseline, Go passed first time): profile show and tui exit 2 within 20-49 ms (profile rows) and 22-28 ms (tui named-pipe row) across the 3 runs for the named pipe, NUL and a directory; Go still opens the named pipe once (pipe_connects 1, final count) before refusing. The three --socket non-endpoints (regular file, directory, non-existent path) give exit 5 AGENT_UNAVAILABLE with nothing modified or created (all asserted from the rows of each run).

limitations: Pass by refusal: the Go prototype can no longer launch ANY .bat or .cmd target, including a bare name resolved through PATHEXT (resolution.pathext_cmd now exit 127). npm-style .cmd shims cannot be run through it. Production remedy (explicit cmd.exe /d /c with a dedicated escaper) is recorded in prototypes/go/REPORT.md as an M01 input. The independent reviewer also showed over-refusal: a real PE image named x.cmd is refused (exit 127), as are 8.3 aliases ending .BAT/.CMD and a literal 'x.bat.' file reached through the \\?\ prefix. Section 9.6 allows refusal.

The refusal is name-based on the path passed to CreateProcess. The reviewer's 30 batch-target probes (ADS spellings, 8.3 names, \\?\ and \\.\ prefixes, hard link and symlink named .exe pointing at a .bat, PATH/PATHEXT bare names, current-directory case) either got the batch refusal or failed to start (127); no argument byte reached cmd.exe. Not probed: whether CreateProcess could match a non-ASCII case-fold variant of .bat/.cmd that Go's strings.ToLower does not fold (reviewer: unlikely, not tested).

Go still opens a named pipe given as --file once (os.Stat before the regular-file check): pipe_connects is 1 in the script rows and the reviewer saw 4 such connections over its profile and tui pipe probes.
